references.text: The sabbatical year for the land is described in detail here, where the earth shall rest every seventh year, and what grows of itself shall be food for all, including the poor and the animals.
God promises blessing in the sixth year to provide for the people through the sabbatical year, demonstrating his care for those who keep the commandment of the sabbatical year.
The sabbatical year also involves the remission of debts, with special emphasis on caring for the poor in the land, which aligns with the concern for the needy in Exodus 23:11.
The command to leave some of the harvest for the poor and the foreigners reflects the same principle of care for the needy as found in the sabbatical year commandment.
Repeats the command to leave some of the harvest for the poor and the foreigners, the same principle of social justice.
Ruth is allowed to glean grain on Boaz's land, illustrating the practice of laws concerning care for the poor.
The people commit themselves to observing the sabbatical year and letting the land rest every seventh year, in accordance with this commandment.
Jesus teaches about God's care for the birds and nature, reflecting the principle that God provides for all creatures, including the animals of the field.
Leviticus 25:4 gives the liturgical definition of the sabbatical year which Exodus 23:11 presupposes in its ethical application.
Nehemiah's confirmation shows that the sabbatical year principle from Exodus remained a central element in God's people's covenant obligations much later.
Leviticus 25:22 resolves the practical problem of food supply that arises when following the commandment in Exodus 23:11.
